body: Evidence is weak-to-negative for autonomous LLM trading and mixed-but-unproven for LLM stock picking. Academic signals (news-sentiment → next-day returns) are real but small, aggregate-only, and partly inflated by memorization/look-ahead bias. Live contests (Alpha Arena) show most LLMs lose money, mainly through overtrading; popular "ChatGPT portfolio beat the market" headlines are short-window paper portfolios with non-comparable rules.
title: ai_tools_workflows › Takeaway

body: "Almost maximum certainty" does not exist in equities. Most individual stocks lose to T-bills over their lifetimes, and all net wealth creation comes from about 4% of stocks. Pros therefore think in probabilities and expected value. They anchor on base rates, size with fractional-Kelly logic (asymmetry times probability, scaled down for estimation error), and pre-commit to kill criteria.
